# Improving without overfitting {#sec-improvements} The report card (@sec-reportcard) showed where the model trails the market. The temptation is to keep trying ideas until one "works". That's how models overfit: with enough tries, something always looks good by luck. So every improvement here follows one rule, written down **before** running anything. ::: {.callout-important} ## The anti-overfitting rule 1. Pre-register a short list of candidates. No trying things until something sticks. 2. Decide on the **2021–2023** out-of-sample seasons only. Adopt a candidate only if its margin error beats the current model in **at least 2 of those 3 seasons** and the paired bootstrap 95% interval of the improvement **excludes zero**. 3. Use **2024–2025** only as a check, never to choose. 4. Log every attempt, including failures, in `docs/experiments/`. 5. The live 2026 season is the real test. ::: ## Preseason information (adopted) The biggest gap was the first weeks of the season: the model knew last year's team, not this year's. Four families of information known **before week 1** were added: | Feature | Source | Idea | |---|---|---| | Transfer portal in/out and net stars | CFBD `/player/portal` (2021+) | Roster turnover | | Recruiting class points, 4-year average | CFBD `/recruiting/teams` | Talent pipeline | | New head coach | CFBD `/coaches` (hire dates) | Coach who starts the season hired in the last 12 months | | Preseason AP poll points | CFBD `/rankings`, week 1 | Expert consensus in August | : Preseason features. Portal entries dated after the season started: at most 0.2%. {#tbl-preseason} | Margin error gap vs the closing line (points) | Before | After | |---|---|---| | 2021–23, weeks 0–2 (decision) | 1.96 | **1.84** | | 2021–23, whole season (decision) | 0.63 | **0.59** | | 2024–25, weeks 0–2 (check) | 1.32 | **1.11** | | 2024–25, whole season (check) | 0.60 | **0.57** | : Random forest, before vs after the preseason features (from `docs/experiments/2026-09-23_preseason_features.md`). {#tbl-preseason-gain} The gap narrows where it was aimed and holds in the check seasons, so the family was adopted. It doesn't close: early in the season the market still knows about quarterback battles, injuries and depth charts. ## Round 2: a more robust model (nothing adopted) ::: {#tbl-round2 .cell tbl-cap='Round 2 candidates. Decision seasons 2021–2023; check seasons 2024–2025.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
Margin 21–23 Total 21–23 O/U 21–23 Margin 24–25 O/U 24–25
A current (RF) 12.82 13.03 50.93 12.53 50.28
B average of 6 12.78 12.89 52.23 12.49 51.60
C dedicated margin/total 12.87 13.01 51.54 12.60 51.22
D = B + C 12.79 12.91 51.36 12.50 51.60
E RF, blowouts clipped 12.85 13.01 50.19 12.54 51.35
``` ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-round2-verdict .cell tbl-cap='Round 2 verdicts under the rule (margin error, decision seasons 2021–2023).' execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
Seasons better (of 3) Gain, 95% interval Adopted
B average of 6 2 [-0.010, +0.108] False
E RF, blowouts clipped 0 [-0.055, -0.002] False
C dedicated margin/total 1 [-0.155, +0.050] False
D = B + C 2 [-0.030, +0.100] False
``` ::: ::: Averaging the six tuned models (B) was best in both periods, but its interval touches zero, so under the rule it isn't adopted. It now runs every week as a **shadow model** (stored, not used for picks) so the 2026 season can settle it. Dedicated margin/total models and clipping blowouts in training were worse. ## Round 3: making recent information count more (nothing adopted) ::: {#tbl-round3 .cell tbl-cap='Round 3 candidates: season recency weights (R1), 30-day form ratings with momentum (R2), both (R3).' execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
Margin 21–23 O/U 21–23 Margin 24–25 O/U 24–25
A current 12.82 50.93 12.53 50.28
R1 recency weights 12.83 49.89 12.59 52.54
R2 form ratings 12.83 50.41 12.53 52.16
R3 R1 + R2 12.86 50.15 12.56 51.85
``` ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-round3-verdict .cell tbl-cap='Round 3 verdicts under the rule (margin error, decision seasons 2021–2023).' execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
Seasons better (of 3) Gain, 95% interval Adopted
R1 recency weights 2 [-0.044, +0.028] False
R2 form ratings 2 [-0.030, +0.026] False
R3 R1 + R2 0 [-0.079, +0.003] False
``` ::: ::: This is what overfitting looks like when you catch it. R1 and R2 look good on the 2024–25 totals (around 52%) but are **worse** on 2021–23 (around 50%). An effect that flips between periods is noise. Choosing from 2024–25 alone would have "improved" the model on paper and hurt it in reality. Recent information already counts at its tuned optimum: the ratings' 120-day half-life beat a 60-day one (@tbl-ridge-grid), and last-3-games and residual-form features already exist. With about 12 games per team, short-term form mostly regresses to the mean. ## Conclusion The remaining gap to the market is **information, not modeling**. What the books know and the model doesn't: the starting quarterback and injuries, the weather for totals, and bowl opt-outs. Those are the next data sources (@sec-roadmap).
